policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the clause: 'and they came unto him, and said, Hail, King of the Jews!' The omission (r01) leaves no coming; the ASV text has it.

ASV opens 'And Pilate went out again' with a bare copulative and no inferential particle; ASV renders οὖν as 'therefore' throughout this chapter (vv. 12, 15, 16, 24), so the absence of 'therefore' here distinguishes καὶ ἐξῆλθεν from Ἐξῆλθεν οὖν.
Pure word order of the same words: 'I find no crime in him' renders either sequence. No mapped textual note.
Ἰδοὺ and Ἴδε are both rendered 'Behold'; ASV's 'Behold, the man!' does not distinguish them. No mapped textual note.

ASV reads 'Crucify him, crucify him!' — an object with each imperative, but only one αὐτόν is at issue, so English must supply an object under either reading. The doubled 'him' therefore does not distinguish the added pronoun.
ASV reads 'We have a law' with no possessive; the added ἡμῶν would give 'our law', which ASV does not render.
Pure word order: 'he made himself the Son of God' renders either sequence of ἑαυτόν and υἱὸν θεοῦ. No mapped textual note.

ASV orders the clauses 'power to release thee, and have power to crucify thee', which excludes the transposed RP sequence (r02) but does not distinguish the base lemma from r01, which carry the same order.
ASV reads 'Jesus answered him'; the indirect object is rendered, which the omission (r01) would not supply.
Pure word order: 'no power against me' renders either sequence. The verse's only note is alternative_rendering ('Or, authority') and does not bear on a reading.
Pure word order of δεδομένον and σοι: 'except it were given thee from above' renders either. No mapped textual note.

Aorist and present substantival participles alike are rendered by an English past relative clause ('he that delivered me unto thee'); ASV renders ὁ παραδιδούς as past elsewhere, so the English does not distinguish the tense here.
Pure word order of subject and verb: 'Pilate sought to release him' renders either. The verse note is alternative_rendering.
ἐκραύγασαν and ἔκραζον are both rendered 'cried out'; ASV's simple past does not distinguish aorist from imperfect here. No mapped textual note.
ASV reads the plural demonstrative, 'heard these words'; r01's singular τοῦτον τὸν λόγον would give 'this word'.
An article after ἐπί is invisible in English; 'sat down on the judgment-seat' renders either. No mapped textual note.
ASV's 'it was about the sixth hour' supplies an English copula and no connective either way; ἦν ὡς and δὲ ὡσεί are alike rendered, ASV regularly leaving δέ untranslated. No mapped textual note.
ASV reads 'They therefore cried out': the inferential 'therefore' renders οὖν, which the RP reading (Οἱ δὲ ἐκραύγασαν) replaces with δέ.
ASV reads 'Then therefore he delivered him' — τότε οὖν; the inferential 'therefore' renders οὖν rather than δέ.
ASV ends the verse at 'to be crucified' with no rendering of the RP addition καὶ ἤγαγον ('and they led him away').

ASV 'bearing the cross for himself' renders the reflexive dative and excludes RP's τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ ('his cross', r02); αὑτῷ and ἑαυτῷ are orthographic variants of the same word and the English cannot distinguish them.

ASV 'unto the place called The place of a skull' has 'place' twice, but the first is an English supply required by the substantival article under the base reading; the wording therefore does not settle whether τόπον stood in the Greek.
The gender of the relative pronoun is invisible in English: 'which is called in Hebrew Golgotha' renders either ὅ or ὅς. No mapped textual note.
ASV lists 'in Hebrew, and in Latin, and in Greek', Latin before Greek, which excludes RP's reversed order (r02) but does not distinguish the base lemma from r01, which share that order.
Pure word order of the copula: 'I am King of the Jews' renders either sequence. No mapped textual note.
ASV reads 'that the scripture might be fulfilled, which saith' — the relative clause ἡ λέγουσα is rendered, and the omission (r01) would leave the citation unintroduced.

ASV reads 'his mother' at both the accusative (τὴν μητέρα, no pronoun in any candidate) and the dative, showing the possessive is supplied from the article; the second 'his' therefore does not distinguish the added αὐτοῦ.
ἴδε and ἰδού are both rendered 'behold'; 'Woman, behold, thy son!' does not distinguish them. No mapped textual note.
Ἴδε and Ἰδού are both rendered 'Behold'; 'Behold, thy mother!' does not distinguish them. No mapped textual note.
ASV reads 'Jesus, knowing that all things are now finished' — εἰδώς; RP's ἰδών would give 'seeing'.
Pure word order of ἤδη and πάντα: 'all things are now finished' renders either sequence. No mapped textual note.

ASV opens the verse 'There was set there a vessel full of vinegar' with no inferential particle, and places its 'so' at the next clause ('so they put a sponge'), where the base text has οὖν; the RP οὖν after σκεῦος is not rendered.

ASV reads 'so they put a sponge full of the vinegar', rendering οὖν and the adjective μεστὸν τοῦ ὄξους with its article; RP's οἱ δὲ πλήσαντες would give a finite participial 'and they filled a sponge'.
ASV reads 'upon hyssop' with no conjunction preceding it; RP's καὶ ὑσσώπῳ would give 'and upon hyssop'.

ASV puts the causal clause first — 'because it was the Preparation, that the bodies should not remain' — which excludes RP's transposed order (r02) but does not distinguish the base lemma from r01, which share that order.
Pure word order of ἤδη and αὐτόν: 'saw that he was dead already' renders either sequence. No mapped textual note.
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are alike rendered 'straightway', and the English adverb's position is governed by English idiom, not the Greek order. No mapped textual note.
Pure word order of copula and pronoun: 'his witness is true' renders either sequence. No mapped textual note.
ASV reads 'that ye also may believe'; the adverbial 'also' renders καί, which r01 omits.
Present and aorist subjunctive alike are rendered 'may believe'; ASV's wording does not distinguish the aspect. No mapped textual note.
ASV 'A bone of him shall not be broken' renders the bare genitive and ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ alike; the note 'Or, crushed' is alternative_rendering and bears on the verb, not this unit.
ASV opens 'And after these things', rendering the connective δέ that r01 omits.
An article before the prepositional phrase is invisible in English: 'Joseph of Arimathaea' renders either. No mapped textual note.
ASV closes 'and took away his body' with a pronoun; RP's τοῦ Ἰησοῦ would give the proper name, 'the body of Jesus', as ASV writes it earlier in the verse where the Greek has the name.
ASV reads 'he who at the first came to him by night' with a pronoun; RP's τὸν Ἰησοῦν would give the proper name.

ASV's text reads 'bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes' (μίγμα) and its textual_variant note, 'Some ancient authorities read roll', relegates ἕλιγμα to the margin; text and note together distinguish the reading.
ASV 'bound it in linen cloths' renders the plain dative and ἐν with the dative alike. No mapped textual note.
ASV's 'wherein was never man yet laid' renders the periphrastic pluperfect and the aorist alike; the English past passive does not distinguish them. No mapped textual note.
